strengths: The conflict and magical fairground escalation begin immediately, with strong comic and visual page-turn energy.
The child tests an imperfect solution, investigates each animal’s need, designs the three-stage approach and leads the climax.
Leo’s force-first instinct, physical strength and capacity to adapt are all plot-essential without displacing the child.
The final slowing sequence pays off the story’s central rhythm play while resolving naturally toward bedtime calm.
mustPreserve: The three distinct rhythms and their connection to the horse, rabbit and duck.
The child-led investigation, rehearsal and lever sequence.
Leo’s shift from blocking or stopping energy to applying precisely measured strength.
The cardboard moon, popcorn and sleepy fairground imagery.
